written.myAnswer: Different compounds have different solubilities because their particles differ. For example, larger sugar molecules can be surrounded by more water molecules than salt ions, so more sugar dissolves.

Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution. As temperature increases, the solubility of most solids in water increases, while the solubility of gases generally decreases.
